rawAnswer: {"story":{"what":"TypeCollector now wraps the analyzer's report callback so that a diagnostic is only reported when its location is in a syntax tree of the compilation being analyzed. Two diagnostic sites that indexed DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] directly (BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull for properties, MemberNeedsKey for fields) now get the location in a null-safe way, so they no longer throw for members that come from metadata. New tests compile a defining assembly to a metadata-only reference, run the analyzers and the generator against code that uses closed generic structs and record structs from that assembly, and check that the resolver is generated. The change also edits MessagePackSecurity.GetEqualityComparer to skip the collision-resistant comparer for string keys, and adds README and MsgPack004 documentation.","why":"For a closed generic type from a referenced assembly, the members come from metadata and have no syntax references.
